fixes.explanation: I get why that sounds right, because land fights are common. But the text never mentions Jephthah keeping any land. The complaint Ephraim states is about not being called: “…without calling us to go with you?” Stick with what the verse says and you'll stay out of trouble.

True. Jephthah says, “My people and I had a serious conflict with the Ammonites, and when I called, you did not save me out of their hands.” So in his telling, he called and Ephraim did not save him. Ephraim asks why he went without calling them, and Jephthah says he did call. That's two very different versions of one phone call.

False is right. The text says Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, fought Ephraim, and “…the men of Gilead struck them down…” Ephraim had come with a threat to burn his house down, and it was Ephraim who was struck down. This part is heavy, baker.

Yes. The verse says it was because the Ephraimites had said, “You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim, living in the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.” That's the insult the text points to. The verse ties those words to the men of Gilead striking Ephraim down.

Fair guess, friend, but leaders aren't what the Ephraimites talked about. What they said, according to the verse, was “You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim, living in the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.” Nothing about leaders in it. That insult was about fugitives.

That's the question at the fords: “Are you an Ephraimite?” The Gileadites have captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim. When a fugitive from Ephraim says, “Let me cross over,” that's what they ask him. It's a simple question, and everything hangs on it.

Amalekites show up in this passage only in 12:15, in the name of the hill country where Abdon is buried. They aren't in the scene at the fords. There the Gileadites ask, “Are you an Ephraimite?” That's the question for that scene.

Not Jephthah, friend. He judged Israel six years, and the verse says he was “…buried in one of the cities of Gilead.” Abdon is the judge buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites (Judges 12:15).

False is right. Jephthah judged Israel six years, and when he died, he was buried “…in one of the cities of Gilead.” That's a city of Gilead, not a burial in Ephraim. The Ephraim burial belongs to Abdon at the end of the passage (Judges 12:15).
